units.text: INT. WOMAN - CONTINUOUS
You have missed not having a father, I suppose, Gerald?
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: Oh, no; my mother has been so good to me. No one ever had such a mother as I have had.
units.name: GERALD

units.text: I am quite sure of that. Still I should imagine that most mothers don’t quite understand their sons. Don’t realise, I mean, that a son has ambitions, a desire to see life, to make himself a name. After all, Gerald, you couldn’t be expected to pass all your life in such a hole as Wrockley, could you?
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: Oh, no! It would be dreadful!
units.name: GERALD

units.text: A mother’s love is very touching, of course, but it is often curiously selfish. I mean, there is a good deal of selfishness in it.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: Slowly .
I suppose there is.
units.name: GERALD

units.text: Your mother is a thoroughly good woman. But good women have such limited views of life, their horizon is so small, their interests are so petty, aren’t they?
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: They are awfully interested, certainly, in things we don’t care much about.
units.name: GERALD

units.text: I suppose your mother is very religious, and that sort of thing.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: Oh, yes, she’s always going to church.
units.name: GERALD

units.text: Ah! she is not modern, and to be modern is the only thing worth being nowadays. You want to be modern, don’t you, Gerald? You want to know life as it really is. Not to be put off with any old-fashioned theories about life. Well, what you have to do at present is simply to fit yourself for the best society. A man who can dominate a London dinner-table can dominate the world. The future belongs to the dandy. It is the exquisites who are going to rule.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: I should like to wear nice things awfully, but I have always been told that a man should not think too much about his clothes.
units.name: GERALD

units.text: People nowadays are so absolutely superficial that they don’t understand the philosophy of the superficial. By the way, Gerald, you should learn how to tie your tie better. Sentiment is all very well for the button-hole. But the essential thing for a necktie is style. A well-tied tie is the first serious step in life.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: Laughing .
I might be able to learn how to tie a tie, Lord Illingworth, but I should never be able to talk as you do. I don’t know how to talk.
units.name: GERALD

units.text: Oh! talk to every woman as if you loved her, and to every man as if he bored you, and at the end of your first season you will have the reputation of possessing the most perfect social tact.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: But it is very difficult to get into society isn’t it?
units.name: GERALD

units.text: To get into the best society, nowadays, one has either to feed people, amuse people, or shock people—that is all!
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: I suppose society is wonderfully delightful!
units.name: GERALD

units.text: To be in it is merely a bore. But to be out of it simply a tragedy. Society is a necessary thing. No man has any real success in this world unless he has got women to back him, and women rule society. If you have not got women on your side you are quite over. You might just as well be a barrister, or a stockbroker, or a journalist at once.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: It is very difficult to understand women, is it not?
units.name: GERALD

units.text: You should never try to understand them. Women are pictures. Men are problems. If you want to know what a woman really means—which, by the way, is always a dangerous thing to do—look at her, don’t listen to her.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: But women are awfully clever, aren’t they?
units.name: GERALD

units.text: One should always tell them so. But, to the philosopher, my dear Gerald, women represent the triumph of matter over mind—just as men represent the triumph of mind over morals.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: How then can women have so much power as you say they have?
units.name: GERALD

units.text: The history of women is the history of the worst form of tyranny the world has ever known. The tyranny of the weak over the strong. It is the only tyranny that lasts.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: But haven’t women got a refining influence?
units.name: GERALD

units.text: Nothing refines but the intellect.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: Still, there are many different kinds of women, aren’t there?
units.name: GERALD

units.text: Only two kinds in society: the plain and the coloured.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: But there are good women in society, aren’t there?
units.name: GERALD

units.text: Far too many.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: But do you think women shouldn’t be good?
units.name: GERALD

units.text: One should never tell them so, they’d all become good at once. Women are a fascinatingly wilful sex. Every woman is a rebel, and usually in wild revolt against herself.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: You have never been married, Lord Illingworth, have you?
units.name: GERALD

units.text: Men marry because they are tired; women because they are curious. Both are disappointed.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: But don’t you think one can be happy when one is married?
units.name: GERALD

units.text: Perfectly happy. But the happiness of a married man, my dear Gerald, depends on the people he has not married.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: But if one is in love?
units.name: GERALD

units.text: One should always be in love. That is the reason one should never marry.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: Love is a very wonderful thing, isn’t it?
units.name: GERALD

units.text: When one is in love one begins by deceiving oneself. And one ends by deceiving others. That is what the world calls a romance. But a really grande passion is comparatively rare nowadays. It is the privilege of people who have nothing to do. That is the one use of the idle classes in a country, and the only possible explanation of us Harfords.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: Harfords, Lord Illingworth?
units.name: GERALD

units.text: That is my family name. You should study the Peerage, Gerald. It is the one book a young man about town should know thoroughly, and it is the best thing in fiction the English have ever done. And now, Gerald, you are going into a perfectly new life with me, and I want you to know how to live.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH
